target_customer: Enterprise customer support and CX teams, mainly in fintech, e-commerce, gaming and fitness tech
problem: Enterprises spend heavily on support agents for repetitive tickets. Early chatbots hallucinated and could not take actions such as refunds or KYC checks.
business_model: Usage-based pricing per resolved ticket (the company site lists $0.49 per resolution), sold to enterprises

founders.name: Deepak Singla
education: IIT Delhi, mechanical engineering with a minor in business management
founders.background_notes: Several years in customer experience and growth at Uber (source: Pulse 2.0 interview). The YC launch post says the founders worked on AI customer interaction systems at Uber, Accenture and PwC.

founders.name: Hakim Khalafi
education: Ecole Polytechnique, master's in engineering mathematics
founders.background_notes: 10+ years in software engineering and analytics per the YC page and Pulse 2.0. The two met at Uber.

investors: Angels from Uber, Intercom, SoftBank, McKinsey and Twitter

technical_complexity.rationale: In 2022 a small team had to build a knowledge-grounded support bot and CRM integrations. The hard parts, accuracy without hallucination and action-taking, came later with agentic LLM stacks.

defensibility.rationale: Helpdesk integrations and customer-specific knowledge give some lock-in, but wrappers around LLMs were easy to copy and the market filled with rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Helpdesk incumbents later shipped their own AI agents, and the company site now compares itself with Intercom Fin, Zendesk AI, Agentforce and Ada. This is a later view, not a source dated at founding.

market_need_then: Support volume and cost were a known enterprise pain point; the founders cite their experience of millions of monthly customer interactions at Uber. The YC launch post pitches real-time answers in 50+ languages and CRM integration in under a week.

branding.domain_note: Operates on usefini.com, not fini.com. The company site states it is unaffiliated with fini.ai or other companies named Fini, and sources note confusion with Intercom's Fin.

identity.mascot_or_character: Third-party review says the agent is named Sophie; not confirmed by company sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Accuracy-first, anti-hallucination positioning; emphasises resolution rate over deflection rate

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself found. The name is short but collides with Fin and other Finis, and the company has to disclaim affiliation on its own site.

pivots.to: Agentic enterprise support agent that takes actions
pivots.why: The company blog says it retired the self-serve chatbot sold in 2023; the Pulse 2.0 interview describes moving from a knowledge bot to action-taking agents.

outcome_analysis: Fini is still active and reached a reported $3.6M seed led by Matrix Partners in January 2026, about three and a half years after YC. Slow funding contrasts with the large AI support market. The founders came from Uber support operations, retired an early self-serve chatbot, and repositioned toward accuracy-first enterprise agents as LLM agents matured. No shutdown, layoff or acquisition reports were found.
notes: The $3.6M figure comes from the Pulse 2.0 article; the CEO said in the interview that the company does not disclose exact amounts. The company blog confirms the lead and participants. An aggregator lists a $500K round in October 2022 (unverified, not recorded). A $125K YC plus Matrix figure from one listing conflicts and is not recorded. A Caplight Series A headline is unrelated. No competitor sources dated at or near the 2022 batch were found; the YC launch post names none.
